newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Aztec bonds likely to be called - Santander.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Aztec bonds likely to be called - Santander.

text.p: Mexico will likely exercise its option to call its Aztec Brady bonds at the end of March, Santander Investment said in a report released on Friday.
"All things considered, if Mexico behaves consistently with its new-found financial sophistication, one would expect that the Aztecs would be called," said Santander analyst Julian Eisner.
Historically, the stripped spread difference between the Mexico Pars and the Aztecs has been about 100-150 basis points.
As the price of the Aztecs began to approach par around Labor Day of 1996, the stripped spread difference began to narrow, "until today it stands at negative 112 basis points," Eisner said.
"This suggests that the value of the call has put a sharp cap on the price appreciation of the Aztecs," he said.

He said that considering that Mexico has just issued ten-year paper at 337 over U.S. Treasuries, the opportunity to save nearly 200 basis points by calling the Aztecs (currently at a stripped spread of 531 basis points) should be "highly attractive."

By calling the Aztecs, Mexico releases the U.S. Treasury zero coupon collateral, which represents almost half the value of the Aztecs, so the issue could be refinanced with a new issuance of only half the size, reducing Mexico's debt by over $1.0 billion, Eisner said.
The Aztec bonds were issued on March 30, 1988.
